title: Options and Keymaps
description: Write your own init.lua: options, the leader key, and keymaps that do what they say.

intro: Your config is a Lua file, usually ~/.config/nvim/init.lua. Options are set through vim.o, so vim.o.number = true is :set number, and keymaps through vim.keymap.set(mode, keys, action, options).
A config runs top to bottom, so anything a later line reads, such as the leader key, has to be set before that line.

commands.text: Set an option: vim.o.relativenumber = true. vim.opt does the same, with methods for list options.
The key <leader> stands for in mappings. Set it before any mapping that uses <leader>.
How many columns >>, << and automatic indenting move by.
Insert spaces instead of a tab character when you press Tab or indent.
With 'ignorecase' on, a search that has a capital letter in it becomes case sensitive.
In a mapping, <cmd>...<CR> runs an Ex command without leaving the current mode or showing the command line.
Describe a mapping in its options: { desc = "Save" }. :map and pickers show it.

levels.title: Relative thinking
levels.description: Keep the absolute line number on the cursor line, and show relative numbers on the others, so counts like 5j can be read straight off the screen.
levels.hint: Duplicate the line with yyp, then insert 'relative' in front of 'number'.

levels.title: Space leader
levels.description: Use <Space> as the leader key. The mapping below should then save on <Space>w.
levels.hint: vim.g.mapleader must be set before the mappings that use <leader>. Here, just change the string: ci" works from anywhere on the line.

levels.title: Two spaces
levels.description: Indent with two spaces: >> on a line should add exactly two.
levels.hint: 'shiftwidth' is the indent step; 'expandtab' makes it spaces.

levels.title: Smart search
levels.description: Searches should ignore case, unless the pattern has a capital letter in it.
levels.hint: 'smartcase' only works together with 'ignorecase'. Duplicate the line and change the option name.

levels.title: Clear the glare
levels.description: Make <Esc> in Normal mode clear the search highlight. The mapping exists, but does nothing yet.
levels.hint: A <cmd>...<CR> right-hand side runs an Ex command without leaving Normal mode: <cmd>nohlsearch<CR>.

levels.title: Say what it does
levels.description: Give the save mapping a description, so :map and which-key style menus can show it.
levels.hint: vim.keymap.set takes an options table as its fourth argument: { desc = "..." }.
